top_story.headline: Lobbyist listing a White House post as a covered position registers $425,000 of quarterly income from two tech clients on 'trade restrictions'
top_story.dek: John McEntee's third-quarter reports show Tencent America and Zhongji Innolight as paying clients.
paragraphs: Two third-quarter reports filed under John McEntee list a combined $425,000 in income. Tencent America LLC, described as a video game and technology company, paid $225,000, and the report gives "No specific issues" under trade. Zhongji Innolight Co. Ltd, described as a maker of optical transceiver modules and interconnects for cloud and AI networks, paid $200,000. Its report says the lobbying concerned "Trade restrictions."
Both filings list McEntee's covered position as "Assistant to the President." The filings do not say which agencies or officials were contacted, and they report no other lobbyists.

Nothing else in today's input is bigger. The two FARA contact-log filings that mention President Donald Trump only reference his policies, not communications with him. The OGE summary describes routine compliance certifications and one ethics agreement with divestitures.

sections.eyebrow: Contacts With the President, VP & Cabinet
sections.headline: No logged FARA contacts with the President, Vice President or cabinet; two LDA reports list the President as lobbied
paragraphs: The two FARA filings flagged this run only mention President Donald Trump in narrative text about Nigeria policy. Neither logs a communication with him. Two third-quarter LDA reports list the President as an entity lobbied.

items: American Library Association (self-filed, 3rd Quarter report): lists the President among the entities lobbied. Issues are appropriations for library agencies and programs, including the Library of Congress, the Government Publishing Office, the Institute of Museum and Library Services and Community Development Block Grants. Filing.

National Cotton Council (self-filed, 3rd Quarter report): lists the President among the entities lobbied and names Keith Sonderling. The filing says the council submitted comments to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative on U.S.-China trade talks and cotton access. It also says it joined a letter urging the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee to advance Sonderling's nomination as Secretary of Labor. Filing.

sections.headline: Three senior appointees file ethics agreements and compliance certifications
paragraphs: New ethics filings from recently confirmed presidential appointees show routine compliance certifications and one ethics agreement with significant divestitures. These documents confirm that appointees are managing potential conflicts of interest through asset disposals and recusals.

items: Laurence Socha, Ambassador to Gambia (Republic of) at the Department of State, filed a Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance on October 22, confirming he has met the terms of his ethics agreement signed June 10, 2026 and effective upon his August 7, 2026 confirmation. Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance.

Anny Vu, Assistant Secretary for Emerging Threats at the Department of State, signed an ethics agreement on August 18, 2026, committing to divest interests in Meta Platforms, Inc., JPMorgan Chase & Co., Apple, Amazon, MicroStrategy Inc., the iShares Semiconductor Fund, and the Rex AI Equity Premium Income Fund—all within 90 days of her confirmation. Until those divestitures are complete, she will recuse from matters directly affecting those companies and funds. Ethics Agreement.

Charles Baldis, Special Counsel at the Office of Special Counsel, filed a Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance on October 21, confirming he has met the terms of his ethics agreement signed June 17, 2026 and effective upon his August 7, 2026 confirmation. Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance.

sections.headline: Two existing registrants add foreign principals: Montenegro's tourism organisation and Japan's Okinawa Prefecture
paragraphs: There are no new registrants or terminations in this window. Two existing registrants took on new foreign principals, and a batch of informational materials, short-form and supplemental filings came in.

items: Miles Partnership, LLLP (#7382) now represents the National Tourism Organisation of Montenegro (Montenegro) as of 10/21/2026. The amendment says the agreement is for public relations services in the U.S. market, with a 12-month term and a total value of EUR 24,990. The Exhibit AB lists Ana Tripkovic Markovic as director. Notice, amendment, Exhibit AB.

Mercury Public Affairs, LLC (#6170) now represents Okinawa Prefecture (Japan) as of 10/20/2026. The amendment says services are expected to include government relations advice, "including possible outreach to US governmental officials." The Exhibit AB gives a contract date of 09/01/2026 and lists Kazuhiro Miyagi, Director of the Military Base Affairs Division, and describes the principal as a local government. The OCR'd signature block reads David Vitter. Notice, amendment, Exhibit AB.

Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.
